6	# Doc migration
7	
8	## Goal
9	A maintenance job that makes the specs the single source of truth for behaviour. Today a feature's behaviour can be described twice — in the doc it was planned from and in the spec that now defines it — and the doc goes stale without anyone noticing. This job goes over the docs against the settled specs, offers to cut what a spec already says, and then offers to turn the feature descriptions that no spec holds yet into specs, each verified against the code on the way through the usual approval check. It never reads code and never rewrites a doc for style: it only removes what is said twice and moves what is said nowhere else into a spec.
10	
11	## Starting the job
12	A maintenance job the person picks when they want the docs and the specs brought back into line, not an errand of the day.
13	
14	- **Maintenance job**: offered on the Maintenance tab of the new-session screen beside *Evaluate docs* and *File decisions*, as a session with the planner's read scope that never reads code (docs/plan-sessions.md#Plan sessions)
15	  - **Nothing counted on the tab**: the tab shows no number for this job, unlike the waiting unfiled decisions (docs/intent/agent.md#Unfiled decisions)
16	- **Settled specs only**: only specs with status approved or implemented are treated as what the product says; a draft spec never costs a doc section
17	- **Outline before judgment**: the job's first pass is the outline of each doc it may read, section by section, and every later judgment is made per section
18	- **Feature content decides scope**: a section is in scope only when its content describes product behaviour; architecture, rationale, guidelines, settings reference and how-to-build sections are out of scope whatever file or folder they sit in
19	- **Confirmed doc writes**: every write into `docs/**` is put to the person first and made only when they say so, one at a time (docs/intent/agent.md#Docs split)
20	- **Setting not consulted**: the job offers its cuts whether or not `kiwiAgent.cutCoveredDocs` is on, since cutting is what it is for (docs/settings.md#Settings)
21	
22	## Pruning what a spec already says
23	The first stage: the doc sections in scope, sorted against the settled specs.
24	
25	- **Covered section**: a section whose behaviour a settled spec now defines is reported with the spec and the rules that cover it, and offered for removal (docs/intent/agent.md#Docs split)
26	  - **Partly covered section**: when only part of a section is covered, what is offered for removal is that part, and the rest is left standing
27	  - **Doc left empty**: a doc with nothing left but its title is offered for deletion together with the index entries and links that point at it
28	- **Contradicting section**: a section that says otherwise than a settled spec is reported and never offered for removal; which side is current is the person's to say (docs/intent/agent.md#Docs split)
29	  - **Contradiction the person rules on**: when they say the doc is current, the ruling is recorded as an unfiled decision naming the feature whose spec it reaches, and the spec is not edited here (docs/intent/agent.md#Unfiled decisions)
30	- **Cited section kept whole**: a section an approved spec's rule cites is not offered for removal without naming the citations that would have to change with it (docs/plan-sessions.md#Finding the way around the docs)
31	- **Nothing covered**: with no covered section found the job says so and goes on to the migration offer
32	
33	## Migrating the remaining feature docs into specs
34	The second stage: the feature descriptions that no spec holds.
35	
36	- **Offered when pruning is settled**: the migration is offered only once no reported covered section is still waiting for an answer
37	- **Feature list first**: the job proposes the features it reads out of the remaining in-scope sections, naming the sections each one comes from, and the person picks which become specs (docs/plan-sessions.md#From a chat)
38	  - **Built or planned**: each proposed feature is marked as behaviour already built or behaviour not yet built, which the person corrects, since it decides what a clean code check means for it
39	- **One draft per pick**: each pick is written as `plan/<feature>.spec.md` with status draft, held to the spec contract, derived from the doc sections alone (docs/plan-sessions.md#Feature planning)
40	- **Source sections left standing**: the sections a draft was written from are not cut by this job; they become covered sections for a later run once that spec is settled
41	- **Reviewed as any draft**: a migrated draft is reviewed and approved in the plan view like any other, and the job never approves one itself (docs/plan-sessions.md#The view)
42	
43	## Verifying a migrated feature against the code
44	What the check against the code means for a spec written from a doc about code that already exists.
45	
46	- **Check on approval**: approving a migrated spec runs the ordinary check against the code, and every disagreement arrives as a decision to rule (docs/plan-sessions.md#The view)
47	- **Clean check on built behaviour**: A spec marked as behaviour already built whose check reports nothing is approved with a task board whose tasks only add the tests that prove its rules, and reaches implemented the usual way once those tests pass.
48	  - **No proofs expected** [removed]
49	  - **Tests without new behaviour**: the tasks of such a board add tests only, and a rule none of the existing behaviour satisfies is reported as a disagreement rather than built here (docs/intent/agent.md#Phase 3: Implement)
50	- **Drift becomes the build**: when the check reports disagreements on built behaviour, rulings, tasks and implementation follow as usual, so only what disagrees gets built (docs/plan-sessions.md#The view)

8	export type Scope = {
9	  /** Globs, workspace-relative, of what Read and Glob may see. */
10	  readable: string[]
11	  /** Globs, workspace-relative, of what Write and Edit may touch. */
12	  writable: string[]
13	  /** Globs a write may reach only with the user's say-so: neither the phase's deliverable nor off limits, so the ordinary permission prompt decides. */
14	  askable?: string[]
15	  /** Globs carved out of `readable`; a match is denied even when readable allows it. */
16	  ignored?: string[]
17	}

19	/**
20	 * Whether a file, workspace-relative, is one the phase may read: the rule Read
21	 * is held to, for a tool that reads files it finds on its own under a path
22	 * the guard already let through.
23	 */
24	export function readableIn(scope: Scope): (relPath: string) => boolean {
25	  return (rel) => !(scope.ignored ?? []).some((g) => matchesGlob(rel, g)) && scope.readable.some((g) => matchesGlob(rel, g))
26	}

28	/**
29	 * Enforces a phase's file scope at the tool call, where the model cannot
30	 * talk its way around it. A blind planner reads the docs and the specs and
31	 * writes one spec; everything else is denied with the reason. A write inside
32	 * the scope is the phase's deliverable, so it goes through without a
33	 * permission prompt.
34	 */
35	export class ScopeGuard implements SessionHooks {
36	  private readonly paths: ProjectPaths
37	
38	  constructor(
39	    cwd: string,
40	    private readonly scope: Scope,
41	  ) {
42	    this.paths = projectPaths(cwd)
43	  }
44	
45	  async preToolUse(tool: ToolUse): Promise<PreToolUseOutcome> {
46	    const input = (typeof tool.input === 'object' && tool.input !== null ? tool.input : {}) as Record<string, unknown>
47	    switch (tool.toolName) {
48	      case 'Read':
49	        return this.check(input['file_path'], this.scope.readable, 'read')
50	      case 'Glob':
51	      case 'Grep':
52	      case MARKDOWN_SEARCH_TOOL:
53	      case CODE_OUTLINE_TOOL:
54	      case CODE_SEARCH_TOOL:
55	        return this.check(input['path'] ?? '.', this.scope.readable, 'search', true)
56	      case 'Write':
57	      case 'Edit':
58	      case 'MultiEdit':
59	        return this.write(input['file_path'])
60	      case 'NotebookEdit':
61	        return this.write(input['notebook_path'])
62	      case 'Bash':
63	      case 'PowerShell':
64	        return { deny: `${tool.toolName} is not available in this phase.` }
65	      default:
66	        return undefined
67	    }
68	  }
69	
70	  /** A deliverable is allowed outright; an askable path is left to the permission prompt; anything else is denied. */
71	  private write(raw: unknown): PreToolUseOutcome {
72	    const denied = this.check(raw, this.scope.writable, 'write')
73	    if (denied === undefined) return { allow: true }
74	    if (this.scope.askable && this.check(raw, this.scope.askable, 'write') === undefined) return undefined
75	    return denied

78	  private check(raw: unknown, globs: string[], verb: string, directory = false): PreToolUseOutcome {
79	    if (typeof raw !== 'string') return { deny: `Cannot ${verb}: no path given.` }
80	    if (!this.paths.inside(raw)) return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} outside the workspace: ${raw}` }
81	    const rel = this.paths.relative(raw)
82	    const ignored = (this.scope.ignored ?? []).find((g) => matchesGlob(rel, g) || (directory && matchesGlob(`${rel}/x`, g)))
83	    if (ignored) return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} ${raw}: excluded from this phase by the ignore setting (${ignored}).` }

85	    // folder a readable glob picks files from: searching from the workspace

87	    // `plan/` beside the specs gives away nothing but the other plan files' names.

90	    if (globs.length === 0) return { deny: `Cannot ${verb} ${raw}: this phase writes nothing.` }

6	/** A doc this short costs less to read whole than to take in two calls. */

11	  "Find before you read docs: MarkdownSearch gives each match with the section it sits in, and Read of a long markdown file answers with its outline first; then Read only the section's line range."

14	 * Answers the first whole-file Read of a long markdown doc with its outline.
15	 * The model reaches for Read, not for a tool it has to remember, so the
16	 * outline is put where it already goes. A second whole-file Read of the same
17	 * doc goes through: the model asked for all of it knowing what that costs.
18	 *
19	 * One gate per session, and it runs after the scope checks, so a doc the
20	 * session may not read is denied by them before its outline is built.
21	 * `exempt` globs name docs that are read whole by design: a spec is the work,
22	 * not a reference to look something up in.
23	 */
24	export class OutlineGate implements SessionHooks {
25	  private readonly outlined = new Set<string>()
26	
27	  constructor(
28	    private readonly cwd: string,
29	    private readonly exempt: string[] = [],
30	  ) {}
31	
32	  async preToolUse(tool: ToolUse): Promise<PreToolUseOutcome> {
33	    if (tool.toolName !== 'Read') return undefined
34	    const input = (typeof tool.input === 'object' && tool.input !== null ? tool.input : {}) as Record<string, unknown>
35	    const raw = input['file_path']
36	    if (typeof raw !== 'string' || !isMarkdown(raw)) return undefined
37	    if (input['offset'] !== undefined || input['limit'] !== undefined) return undefined
38	    const path = isAbsolute(raw) ? raw : resolve(this.cwd, raw)
39	    if (this.outlined.has(path)) return undefined
40	    const rel = relative(this.cwd, path).split('\\').join('/')
41	    if (this.exempt.some((glob) => matchesGlob(rel, glob))) return undefined
42	    // An unreadable file is Read's to report.
43	    const text = await readFile(path, 'utf8').catch(() => undefined)
44	    if (text === undefined || markdownLines(text).length <= OUTLINE_THRESHOLD_LINES) return undefined
45	    this.outlined.add(path)
46	    return {
47	      deny: [
48	        formatOutline(raw, text),
49	        '',
50	        'This doc is long, so here is its outline instead of the text. Read the section you need with offset (its first line) and limit (its line count). Read the file again without offset and limit only if you need all of it.',
51	      ].join('\n'),
